title: Well-formedness of the block tree construction
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on $n$ sign variables, let $f$ be a natural-number fuel value, and let $\rho$ be a coordinate restriction. If every coordinate free in $\rho$ belongs to a specified set of available coordinates, then the tree constructed from $\varphi$, $f$, and $\rho$ is well formed relative to that set: each queried coordinate is available at its node, and both child trees are well formed relative to the available set with that coordinate removed.
hypotheses_covered: A disjunctive normal form on those coordinates
Every coordinate free in the restriction lies in the available set
